_verification_note: Verification is scaled to a diff that contains zero TypeScript and zero product code. `pnpm -r run test` (the third leg of `pnpm test`) exercises packages this diff does not touch, needs a live Postgres, and is a measured flake source on a shared cluster. kit:check and test:review-readiness are both legs of `pnpm test` and both DO cover this diff: the first proves the two new scripts/ files are classified, the second proves the new test file is actually registered and RUNS rather than merely existing -- verify that property by checking the runner's total falls when scripts/db-reset-test.test.mjs is removed from the `test:review-readiness` list, not by comparing against a number written here. The happy path WAS exercised once end to end on v2's equivalent tree: plexco_test was dropped and recreated, then the @plexco/db suite ran green on the rebuilt database (13 files, 716 tests), which is what proves recovery rather than mere deletion.

security_review.reason: the script executes DROP DATABASE against a live cluster, so the trust boundary is everything that decides WHICH database is destroyed. After the v3 redesign that is no longer the connection string: DATABASE_URL_TEST is demoted to a database-name cross-check, and the tool owns its own target -- the docker endpoint (verified to be a local unix socket, because the active context lives in ~/.docker/config.json and stripping environment variables does not neutralise it), the compose project (pinned with -p, with COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME removed from the child environment), the container, the executing role (always passed as -U, so no layer below supplies a competing default) and the database name. Look there. Two things this is NOT, both of which have already misdirected a reviewer once: there is no shell-injection surface (spawnSync with an argv array, no shell), and connection-string parsing is no longer an authority, so URL-grammar findings are out of contract. Remaining SQL surface is identifier handling, addressed by the plain-identifier rule, the 63-byte limit and quoting. NOTE: the hash-locked runtime manifest still carries the pre-redesign wording naming the connection string as the real surface; it cannot be edited in place, and the readiness gate excludes this field from the authored/runtime comparison. It is also never transmitted to the reviewer -- autopilot-review-readiness.mjs builds the security prompt as a fixed string -- so this field informs humans, not the security round.

Compare by exclusion: `jq 'walk(if type == "object" then with_entries(select(.key | test("^_") or . == "manifest_schema_version" or . == "review_gate_version" | not)) else . end) | .security_review.reason = null'` on both, then compare the two outputs.
